codes.name: The Provenance Ledger
codes.short_def: Human-made value claimed not through imagery but through metadata performed as form: museum-grade captions, credit blocks set as typographic objects, supply-chain disclosure, and the ritualized consent line ('shared with permission') that extends provenance to the image's right to exist. Verbally it runs on forensic vocabulary.
codes.one_liner: Documentation is the aesthetic: credits, captions, materials, dimensions, and consent lines do the certifying.
codes.definition: The strongest pattern in the corpus. Human-made value is claimed not through imagery but through metadata performed as form: museum-grade captions (title, year, materials, dimensions), full credit blocks set as typographic objects, supply-chain disclosure, and the newly ritualized consent line ('All images courtesy of the artist, shared with permission'), which extends provenance from the object to the image's right to exist, a quiet anti-scraping ethic. Verbally it runs on forensic vocabulary: evidence, detection, audit, receipts, scare quotes around 'writers'.

composition: metadata framed as part of the artwork's field
casting_setting: the maker named, the chain of custody visible: photographer, stylist, permission

metaphors: forensics and exposure: catching, testing, digging for wires
verbal.register: forensic, prosecutorial, cool enumeration then verdict

sample_phrases.quote: the era of evidence is over, and there is only content
Some of the biggest 'writers' on Substack aren't writing at all.
It's now a brand name, he insists, with nothing behind it.

codes.tensions: Defines itself against the unsourced, the laundered byline, institutions that defected (Sports Illustrated, prize juries). Internal critique (Horning): when evidence becomes content, receipts themselves become a style that can be worn.
codes.execution_notes: Cheapest code to execute and the hardest to fake retroactively: publish the chain of custody (who made it, of what, when, with whose permission) as designed form, not legal fine print. Misuse: provenance theater on an industrially produced product reads as the Liffner grid next to the one hand-woven bag, the audience notices the intruder.

codes.name: Countable Labor
codes.short_def: Human labor certified by making its units countable. Visually: the macro detail where a single loop, stitch or fold is legible (the 'Detail of…' convention), and the wide shot of a vast field of small handmade units. Verbally: quantified duration and volume as watermark, '22 years', 'thousands of strips', 'hand-cut', shot in clinical verification light.
codes.one_liner: Authentication by enumeration: the stitch macro, the field of ten thousand units, the headline that counts the years.
codes.definition: Human labor certified by making its units countable. Visually: the macro detail where the loop, stitch, silk strip, or fold-line is individually legible (institutionalized as the full-work-then-'Detail-of' layout convention), and the wide shot of a vast field of small handmade units (a 50-foot miniature city, thousands of silk tabs, clustered embroidery hoops). Verbally: quantified duration and volume as watermark, '22 years', 'thousands of strips', 'hand-cut'. Shot in clinical, shadowless verification light on gallery grounds, museum grammar applied to humble materials.

materials_textures: yarn, silk strips, punch-needle, machine-knit with seams showing
casting_setting: the work, not the worker; labor present as accumulation rather than action

sample_phrases.quote: If you take money for work you didn't do yourself, then you are a thief.
people find a unique comfort in art that feels clearly and intentionally made by human hands

codes.tensions: Against instantaneous slickness and infinite reproduction; the unit that took time vs the output that took none. Watch: the labor proof has migrated from imagery into captions and headlines, working hands are nearly absent (1 of 83 images), so the counting is increasingly taken on faith.
codes.execution_notes: For brands: show the unit of making at watermark fidelity (the loop, the weld, the brushstroke) and let the numbers be specific and checkable. Misuse: counting things that aren't labor ('1,000 hours of testing' on an automated process) imports the form without the referent, and this audience audits.

codes.name: The Unretouched Witness
codes.short_def: A person, or the trace of one, does the certifying. Three carriers: the dead-frontal face marked by a life (tattoos, age, stage blood); casting older and realer than fashion default; and the snapshot vernacular, hard flash and clutter left in frame, where imperfection proves nothing was staged. Verbally it claims the unforgeable: flesh, mortality, the cultivated ear ('I can tell'), disgust at the synthetic as proof of humanity.
codes.one_liner: Imperfect human presence as the logo: life-marked faces, mature casting, hard flash, clutter left in frame.
codes.definition: A person, or the unmistakable trace of one, does the certifying. Three carriers: the dead-frontal face bearing permanent marks of a life (tattoos, age, stage blood); casting that runs older and realer than fashion default; and the snapshot vernacular, hard on-camera flash, mirrors, fire extinguishers and garment bags left in frame, where photographic imperfection itself testifies that nothing was staged. Verbally it claims the unforgeable: flesh, mortality, appetite, the cultivated ear ('I can tell'), and visceral disgust at the synthetic as a bodily, pre-rational proof of humanity.

composition: dead-frontal portrait, face as full bleed
typography: minimal; the face replaces the wordmark
casting_setting: face tattoos, mature models (40s+), maker's own selfie, opera performer with blood trickle: the specific person, not the type

lexicon: 活人感 huo ren gan ('living-person feel', the uncurated self)
metaphors: body as credential: mortality, appetite, addiction as the unforgeable watermark
verbal.register: threat-comic oath of discernment; visceral; tender-deadpan

sample_phrases.quote: Did you think I wouldn't be able to tell? I can tell.
This was a living creature. Let's not waste it.
However bad a writer you think you are, you are not worse than AI.
a new standard for authenticity, the quality of feeling genuinely, unpolishedly alive
反精致 is the pushback: intentionally rough, unstaged, and unbothered

codes.tensions: Against the idealized, the retouched, the synthetic spokesperson, and the fashion-blank face. Internal anxiety: every witness-mark is counterfeitable (a filter can fake flash; AI can fake a face), so the code keeps retreating toward the genuinely unforgeable: age, mortality, named specific people.
codes.execution_notes: Casting and registration ARE the strategy: specific, named, life-marked people shot frontally with their context left in frame. Misuse: 'real people' casting with retouched skin and cleared sets reads as the fashion-blank deadpan it replaced, the audience reads light and clutter before they read faces.

evidence.note: face-tattooed frontal portrait, face as full bleed: the face is the product
mature casting (40s+), weathered mastery, film-soft light
hard flash, mirrors, fire extinguisher and garment bags in frame: snapshot vernacular as certificate

codes.name: Slop, Repainted Slow
codes.short_def: Cheap circulation re-made expensive: oil paintings of phone screenshots that keep the title bar, airbrushed memes, collagraphs printed from discarded cartons with the dielines as skeleton. The acid slop palette is quoted as subject matter while the slow medium does the certifying. Verbally, the 'slop' word-family at full inflection, and the corpus's sharpest fight: every authenticity move is gameable.
codes.one_liner: Disposable detritus, screenshots, memes, shipping cartons, lovingly re-rendered in slow media with its artifacts preserved.
codes.definition: The emergent and most contested code: cheap circulation re-made expensive. Oil paintings of phone screenshots that keep the caps-lock title bar; airbrushed meme cats; collagraphs printed FROM discarded cartons with dielines and glue-tabs as the composition's skeleton; a Sufi saint's archival photo woodcut onto a to-go cup. The acid slop palette appears inside the work, quoted as subject matter, while the medium does the certifying. Verbally this is the 'slop' word-family at full inflection (slopified, tasteslop, corporate slop) and the corpus's sharpest internal fight: the awareness that every authenticity move is gameable.

composition: UI chrome as framing device (title bars, captions, watermarks kept)
detritus silhouette as the picture's structure
typography: meme caption faces rendered in slow media
casting_setting: the internet's cast: Trisha Paytas, filter bunnies, WhatsApp chickens, elevated to portrait subjects

metaphors: food and contamination: swill, ingestion, 'eat this up'
magic and possession: the demon, the bluff, the hallucination
verbal.register: ironic-devotional; the anti-romantic skeptic policing its own moves

sample_phrases.quote: Tasteslop is cultural capital after extraction, after it's been through the blender.
Producing intentionally flawed content to assert one's humanity is like solving an elaborate CAPTCHA.
Like any LLM output, A.I.-generated images are designed to please, not to provoke.
Slop's dismissibility is part of its appeal

codes.tensions: Against slickness itself, not just machines (slop predates AI: Shein, private equity media). And against its own gameability: the 'lo-fi tryhard', intentional jank as Instagram filter, liminal-horror CGI wearing craft language. This code knows it can be counterfeited and makes that knowledge part of the work.
codes.execution_notes: The highest-risk, highest-reward register: it requires the brand to display taste ABOUT the slop economy it operates in, naming the cheap thing while making it expensively. Misuse is fatal here: doing this without genuine wit produces exactly the tasteslop it critiques, and this audience coined the word for it.

codes.name: The Analog Sanctuary
codes.short_def: The oldest code, tagged residual: inhabited spaces built around analog ritual, vinyl walls, turntable altars, film cameras in working hands, long tables of people journaling by window light. Lit warm and practical, never HDR. What clients reach for by default when briefed 'human', though its smartest advocates concede the memory is partly reinvented, not remembered.
codes.one_liner: Warm-lit rooms where slow media is practiced together: the listening bar, the record shop, the reading cafe, the archive as altar.
codes.definition: The oldest and most familiar code, tagged honestly as residual: inhabited spaces organized around analog ritual, vinyl walls and turntable altars, film cameras in working hands, long tables of people journaling by window light, lived-in interiors of wood, plaster, and glass. Lit warm and practical (lamps, candles, low winter sun, film stock), never HDR. This is what clients reach for by default when briefed 'human', and it still works, but its smartest advocates concede its memory is partly synthetic: its young consumers 'aren't remembering it, they are reinventing it'.

composition: shelf and archive walls as backdrop
typography: spine labels, obi strips, hand-lettered signage
casting_setting: people mid-practice: listening, reading, journaling, digging through crates; the owner who knows the stock

metaphors: the soul of the past preserved
verbal.register: devotional, tactile-reverent, elegiac at the edges

sample_phrases.quote: preserving the raw, tactile soul of the past

codes.tensions: Against the placeless, the streamed, the frictionless. Internal critique (Horning): nostalgia for the golden age of 'seeing is believing' is partly reactionary, and the sanctuary is increasingly a reinvention rather than a memory, which is why it reads residual, not emergent.
codes.execution_notes: Safe, legible, and aging: right for spaces, retail, and hospitality where the practice is real (an actual listening bar, an actual archive). Misuse: applying sanctuary set-dressing to a digital-first product is the most common 'certified human' cliche in client work, and the one this corpus's writers mock most readily.

counterexample: Dataland names a gallery 'The Sanctuary' and pipes in forest scent, the machine borrowing the sanctuary's own vocabulary

'Militant Chemistry' -- the material substrate of analog film: the Kodak/Agfa chemical-industry sites that made film stock possible.
